pages.text: The lab reports nutrients in $(thing)ppm$() in the top 20 cm, as a real soil laboratory does. Rough guides:$(li)$(thing)N$() (nitrate): under 10 low, 20-40 optimum.$(li)$(thing)P$(): under 10 low, 20-40 optimum.$(li)$(thing)K$(): under 90 low, 130-200 optimum.

$(li)$(thing)pH$(): 6.0-7.0 suits most crops.$(li)$(thing)Organic matter$(): 3% or more is healthy. It feeds nitrogen and holds water.$(li)$(thing)CEC$(): higher means the soil holds nutrients and resists pH change.

$(thing)Water$() is shown as the volume fraction $(thing)θ$() next to field capacity (full after drainage) and wilting point (empty to plants). $(thing)Compaction$() above about 40% restricts roots and drainage; ploughing breaks it up.
